title: Math with Variables
story: You're at the corner store buying snacks for a movie night. You grab 3 bags of chips at $4 each and 2 sodas at $2 each. Instead of doing the math in your head, you let your program figure out the total!
why: Programs that calculate with variables can handle any numbers you throw at them — making them flexible and reusable.
analogy: Variables in math are like labeled jars — you put numbers in, do operations with the labels, and get new numbers out.
try_it: Calculate the total cost of 3 pizzas at $12 each. Create a `price` variable set to 12 and a `quantity` variable set to 3, then multiply and print!
tips: Always declare the type of your variable: `let total: Int = price * quantity;`
Use descriptive names like `price` and `quantity` instead of `a` and `b`
The result of math goes into a NEW variable — don't try to change a `let` variable
common_mistakes: Forgetting the semicolon at the end of each line — every statement in XIOM needs one!
Using `x` instead of `*` for multiplication — `x` is just a letter, `*` is the multiply sign
